The n=512 batch=640 shapes are ~70% of the benchmark (~940k us each, 4 variants). Replace cuSOLVER's tens-of-thousands of tiny launches with a batched BLOCKED Householder QR in pure FP32: a custom panel kernel factors a block of 32-64 columns (one CTA per matrix, shared memory) producing reflectors V and tau, build the block reflector T (larft), then apply (I - V T V^T) to the trailing submatrix via cublasSgemmStridedBatched across all 640 matrices at once. Collapse the launch count to O(n/block) batched GEMMs + panel kernels. Land this dominant shape first; fallback elsewhere.

Blocked Householder QR for n=512: custom panel kernel (1 CTA/matrix, shared mem, BLK=32) producing V/tau/T, trailing update via torch.bmm/baddbmm (cublasSgemmStridedBatched). Dispatch by size n==512, else torch.geqrf. Geomean 112275.78->39876.67 us (2.82x); n=512 b=640 shapes ~940k->~42k us each (~22x). Validates clean incl all 3 guards.

Panel kernel: warp-parallel reflector apply (each warp owns strided trailing cols, __shfl reductions) replacing the per-column serial block-sync loop; larfg norm via warp shuffle. BLK=32 (best divisor fitting 99KB shared opt-in; 16 slower, >=48 too big). n=512 shapes ~42.8k->~35.8k us. Geomean 39876.67->37730.56 us (2.97x vs baseline). Clean incl all guards.

Panel kernel 1024 threads/CTA: ncu showed latency-bound (SM 5.3%, 1 block/SM, only 8 warps at 256 thr). 1024 thr = 32 warps hides the sequential larfg chain. Swept 256/512/768/1024, 1024 best. n=512 shapes ~35.8k->~30.4k us. Geomean 37730.56->35732.05 us (3.14x vs baseline). Clean incl all guards.

Panel kernel: build T (larft) from the hot shared panel + warp-parallel z reductions, replacing uncoalesced global-Vm strided reads with serial thread-starved z loops. Big hidden cost removed. n=512 shapes ~30.4k->~16.7k us (~1.8x). Geomean 35732.05->29237.15 us (3.84x vs baseline; n=512 ~57x vs 941k baseline). Clean incl all guards.

Two-level blocking: factor each 64-wide super-block as 2 shared-resident BLK=32 panels + inner update, assemble combined 64-wide V and T64=[[T_A,T_AB],[0,T_B]], do ONE 64-wide batched trailing GEMM. Halves the (now-dominant) trailing-GEMM count with better contraction width. n=512 shapes ~16.7k->~14.9k us. Geomean 29237.15->28083.64 us (4.00x vs baseline). Clean incl all guards.

Two-level: panel kernel writes clean V directly into the wide SB=64 V64 buffer via (ld,row,col) offsets, removing per-super-block host-side reflector copies; T assembled in place. n=512 shapes ~14.9k->~14.1k us. Geomean 28083.64->27616.39 us (4.07x vs baseline). Validates clean incl all 3 guards.

Retune panel threads/CTA 1024->512 (eval-confirmed; balance shifted after the shared T-build cut panel cost). n=512 shapes ~14.1k->~12.9k us. Geomean 27616.39->26835.18 us (4.18x vs baseline). Clean incl all guards.
Eval-swept NTHREADS optimum: {256,384,512,1024} -> 384 best. n=512 shapes ~12.8k us. Geomean 26835.18->26774.83 us (4.20x vs baseline). Clean incl all guards.

DELIVERED the n=512 blocked Householder QR brief: geomean 112393->26775 us (4.20x; best commit 3d9a967a). The 4 n=512 b=640 shapes went ~941k->~12.8k us each (~73x per-shape); all dense/mixed/rankdef/clustered. Validates clean on every iteration incl. all 3 anti-reward-hack guards (diff-correctness 8 inputs/shape, invariance sweep to batch=1280 + ill-cond fraction/position, off-grid-n). Genuine compact-Householder output (FP32, backward-stable); dispatch strictly by size n==512 else torch.geqrf.

DESIGN: custom CUDA panel kernel (load_inline), one CTA/matrix, panel column-major in shared, warp-parallel reflector apply + larfg via __shfl. Builds larft T from the HOT shared panel (NOT global) -- this was the single biggest win (3.14x->3.84x): the original global-Vm strided/thread-starved T-build was a huge hidden cost. Two-level blocking: factor each 64-wide super-block as 2 shared-resident BLK=32 sub-panels + small inner update, assemble combined 64-wide V (kernel writes V straight into the wide buffer via ld/row/col offsets, no host copies) and T64=[[T_A,T_AB],[0,T_B]], then ONE 64-wide cublasSgemmStridedBatched (torch.bmm/baddbmm) trailing update. NTHREADS=384/CTA (eval-swept).

WHAT DIDN'T WORK: (a) panel in L2-global instead of shared -> much slower (L2 re-stream beats shared reuse); (b) row-tiled 'balanced' apply -> slower than warp-per-column; (c) TF32 trailing GEMM -> NO speedup AND scaled factor residual jumped ~0.01->15 (near the 20 limit), rejected; (d) NSUB=4 super-block (SB=128) -> more bmm launch overhead outweighs the wider-GEMM saving. BLK is capped at 32 by the 99KB shared opt-in (BLK>=48 doesn't fit a full 512-row panel); two-level is how I got 64-wide GEMMs anyway.

CURRENT BOTTLENECK: the trailing cuBLAS FP32 GEMM is now the floor (~half of timed GPU work; panel kernel is only ~3% of the checker-dominated nsys). Hard to beat further in FP32.

Suggest a fresh macro brief: extend the blocked path to n in {1024,2048,4096} (all divisible by 32) with a height-capped shared panel. That is likely a larger geomean win than anything left on n=512.
